title: Insurance Claim Repairs Production Standard — Drop-Off to Vehicle-Ready
content:
## Drop-off and start of work

Work on an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order starts when the vehicle is dropped off after authorization. At drop-off the class's number of walk-around photos and the odometer reading are recorded, a pre-repair scan is run where the class requires one, and a hybrid or electric vehicle is depowered where the class requires high-voltage depower.

Where the class requires the non-original parts disclosure and the insurer's estimate specifies non-original parts, the customer's non-original parts disclosure on the repair order is signed before work starts.

## During the repair

- Parts follow the class's original-equipment parts requirement and its recycled-parts allowance.
- The customer is updated at least once in every span of the class's update interval, counted in business days, through the class's status update channel.
- The class's target cycle time is a planning target, not a promise.
- A courtesy ride is offered within the class's courtesy ride radius of the center.

## Vehicle-ready notice

The vehicle-ready notice requires, as the class sets them: the post-repair scan where required, the four-wheel alignment check where required, the class's number of structural measurement reports, a road test of the class's road-test miles, and the class's quality-checkpoint inspection.

In addition, every calibration order linked to the repair order is completed or its declination is signed. This is read from the ADAS Sensor Calibrations orders linked to the repair order and their declination records, before the vehicle-ready notice issues.

| Calibration order linked to the repair order | Declination | Counts as closed for vehicle-ready |
|---|---|---|
| completed | — | Yes |
| not completed | signed | Yes |
| not completed | not signed | No |
| no calibration order linked | — | nothing to close |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical repair orders)

- Two calibration orders are linked; one is completed and the other's declination is signed — every linked order is closed.
- Two calibration orders are linked; one is completed and the other is open with no signed declination — the vehicle-ready notice does not issue.
- A Standard Claim Repair vehicle with an unsigned non-original parts disclosure, where the insurer's estimate specifies non-original parts — work does not start.
